A few questions about gaming on linux, wine , playonlinux and how to get stuff running

Regarding Wine versions: Playonlinux can manage multple versions of Wine at the same time - each game you have configured in POL is set to use a specific versions. Which is nice, because some games only work with a specific Wine version.

Also, POL manages these versions in a different way from your normal Software center (or whatever Mint uses to install packages), so you won't find all of those versions there. Use POL to manage them.

To see which versions are installed, go to Tools (in the top menu) -> Manage Wine versions. (Note that it takes a few seconds to load.) There are two tabs, one for 32-bit variants (x86) and one for 64-bit variants (amd64). To install an additional version, just select it in the left pane and use the arrow thingy to move it to the right one; you'll get a pop-up with essentially an installation wizard.

To change which Wine version a specific game uses, click the game's name in the main POL window, and click Configure on top. In the new window, go to the General tab, and look for the "Wine version" drop-down; you can choose from all versions you have installed, or press + to go to the management interface and install additional versions.

Regarding Mass Effect and FF XIV, unfortunately I have no idea, I never tried running either of those. You could try checking winehq and searching for your game. A lot of the time people leave useful info - what they did to get it running; you can get to it by first selecting the version of the game at the bottom of the page I linked, and then you pick a "Test result" for a system which preferably matches yours. If that's not possible, try to get the closest match (for Mint it wouild be anything from the Ubuntu or Debian family).

Well, it's not a requirement with WineHQ to post a specific walkthrough. The site doesn't focus that, only on results. Still, some people are kind enough to include what they did when they post a result - it doesn't work every time, but it happens fairly often. For example, the HOWTO part here.

With Origin... that's gonna be a bit of a problem, unfortunately. It's much newer and less popular than Steam so people don't test it as much. It even seems that POL doesn't have a script for it, so that sucks. Apparently the installation of Origin itself doesn't work reliably; someone posted a workaround, but it requires that you have access to a Windows install... https://appdb.winehq.org/objectManager.php?sClass=version&iId=26175&iTestingId=89069

Generally, here's what I would try: I would attempt to install Origin itself first into a separate POL virtual drive. Once Origin works, I would only use this instance to download one single game (e.g. only Mass Effect and nothing else); if I wanted a second game I'd install Origin again and keep it separate, because the other games will likely need different settings. Once Origin downloads the game, I would go into settings for that particular Origin install and add any additional components (directx, .net, etc.) that the game needs, and make any additional changes (make it use a specific Wine version if needed, etc.).

You can often find a list of these components on WineHQ (for example, someone says they got it running when they installed "d3dx9 msie corefonts dotnet40" - those are all components). If you have a list of components you need to use, you can install them by selecting the game (or Origin installation) in the main POL window, then Configure -> Install components tab.

You should be able to install and run Origin through Wine and then install Mass Effect through the Origin client as you would on Windows.

You can run Wine from the terminal, as in wine Setup.exe, for example. Everything you install goes under ~/.wine/drive_c/ from where you would cd to the correct subdirectory and run the program with wine nameofprogram.exe. There are probably some graphical tools for launching and managing your Wine programs, but this is the basic way to do it.

PlayOnLinux lets you pick a Wine version and configuration for each program separately, so whatever you install with PlayOnLinux you would also also run from PlayOnLinux.

There's no need for you to find that directory, and Setup.exe was just an example. When you download an installer for a Windows program you can run it from ~/Downloads or wherever you've put it, and once the program is installed (likely somewhere under ~/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/) you'll need to find the correct .exe there.

If there's no ~/.wine/drive_c, running winecfg should generate it.
